opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Facility Condition Assessment and Asset Management Solution
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (County) is soliciting competitive proposals from qualified firms to deliver a turnkey Facility Condition Assessment (FCA), compile a unified Master Equipment Register (MER), deploy an enterprise-grade cloud Facility Condition Information System (FCIS), and implement bi-directional integration with the County’s Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) IBM Maximo Application Suite SaaS. This solicitation is structured into two distinct operational phases: PHASE 1 (BASE SCOPE) : Complete on-site baseline Facility Condition Assessments across approximately 100 facilities (~4.5 million gross square feet across 75 sites) following ASTM E2018-24 standards. Perform discrete equipment nameplate inventories and install durable 2D physical barcode tags for maintainable mechanical, electrical, plumbing, conveyance, and life-safety systems. Compile and validate a unified Master Equipment Register (MER) that establishes an identical data baseline between IBM Maximo and the FCIS. Provide, configure, and host a SaaS-based FCIS platform delivering real-time Facility Condition Index (FCI) calculations, multi-year capital renewal modeling, and localized RSMeans-based cost estimating. Format, validate, and batch-load the complete Master Equipment Register directly into the County’s IBM Maximo Application Suite environment, and establish automated synchronization between Maximo and the FCIS. PHASE 2 (OPTIONAL/ADD-ALTERNATIVE SCOPE): Develop standard, manufacturer-aligned Preventive Maintenance (PM) Job Plans, task check-sheets, and recommended service frequencies, pre-formatted for direct batch upload into Maximo Job Plans and PM Master applications.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Project Management Services
opportunities.description: The County’s objective in issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) is to establish agreements with one or more qualified contractors to provide project management, project implementation, and related consulting services on an as-needed basis. Services may support a range of County initiatives, including the planning, design, procurement, implementation, integration, and rollout of software-as-a-service (SaaS) and other technology systems, as well as non-technology operational, organizational, and business-process improvement projects. Selected contractor(s) may be engaged to provide experienced project managers and related subject-matter support to lead or augment County project teams, develop and maintain project plans and governance structures, coordinate stakeholders and vendors, manage risks, issues, schedules, budgets, communications, change management, and implementation activities, and otherwise support successful project delivery. The County does not guarantee a minimum volume of work; specific assignments within the scope of this RFP, duration, and staffing needs will be established through individual contracts. The County’s standard contract template is included as an appendix to this solicitation. Awarded contractor(s) will be expected to enter into an agreement prepared by the County using this template. Proposers should ensure that their firms have completed legal review of the contract terms before submitting a proposal. If a proposer wishes to request exceptions to the County’s standard terms, it must submit a Contract Exceptions Request by the Deadline for Questions, Comments, and Contract Exceptions identified in the Solicitation Schedule. The County will consider requested exceptions but reserves the right to reject proposed modifications to its standard contract terms.

opportunities.title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Quality Assurance Testing Services
opportunities.description: The County’s objective in issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) is to establish agreements with one or more qualified contractors to provide quality assurance (QA), testing, and related consulting services on an as-needed basis in connection with software and related technology used by the County. Services may support a range of County initiatives, including the planning, design, implementation, integration, enhancement, and ongoing maintenance of software-as-a-service (SaaS) and other technology systems, as well as other County applications, business processes, and operational initiatives requiring structured testing and quality assurance support. Selected contractor(s) may be engaged to provide experienced QA testers, test leads, and related subject-matter support to lead or augment County project teams. Services may include developing and executing test strategies, test plans, test cases, test scripts, and test data; conducting functional, regression, integration, system, user acceptance, accessibility, performance, and other appropriate testing; documenting and tracking defects; coordinating testing activities among County staff, vendors, and other stakeholders; validating defect resolutions; supporting user acceptance testing; and providing testing status reports, recommendations, and other deliverables necessary to support successful project implementation and system quality. The County does not guarantee a minimum volume of work; specific assignments within the scope of this RFP, duration, and staffing needs will be established through individual contracts. The County’s standard contract template is included as an appendix to this solicitation. Awarded contractor(s) will be expected to enter into an agreement prepared by the County using this template. Proposers should ensure that their firms have completed legal review of the contract terms before submitting a proposal. If a proposer wishes to request exceptions to the County’s standard terms, it must submit a Contract Exceptions Request by the Deadline for Questions, Comments, and Contract Exceptions identified in the Solicitation Schedule. The County will consider requested exceptions but reserves the right to reject proposed modifications to its standard contract terms.

opportunities.title: Power Delivery General Engineering Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena is seeking qualified professional engineering firms to supplement its internal resources within the Water and Power Department (PWP), Power Delivery Division. Engineering services provided under the resulting contracts will support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation, maintenance, modernization, and improvement of PWP's electric power delivery system. Engineering services under this RFP are organized into the following Scope of Work Groups: Receiving Station and Substation Design SCADA, Automation, Communications, and Control Design System Planning Civil and Structural Engineering Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Renewable Energy, Energy Storage, Interconnection, and Technical Advisory Services Associated services, including construction management, inspection, drafting, and other technical support, may be required as part of an individual task order where applicable to the assigned Scope of Work Group. Engineering services under the resulting contracts are intended to supplement, not replace, PWP's internal engineering resources. Consultants may be assigned work based on project-specific needs, staff availability, schedule requirements, temporary workload conditions, and the need for specialized expertise. All consultant designs and deliverables shall be subject to review and approval by the responsible PWP engineering group. Consultants shall not supervise City employees or exercise project management authority over City staff. Work that is ongoing, predictable, or programmatic over multi-year periods will generally be performed by permanent PWP staff. The City intends to award multiple contracts under this solicitation to establish a pool of qualified engineering consultants. Work will be authorized through individual task orders based on the requirements of the assignment, including consultant availability, applicable expertise, capacity, schedule, and other considerations identified by the City. Award of a contract does not guarantee any minimum quantity or value of work. Current priority programs anticipated for consultant support include, but are not limited to: SCE Upgrade of the TMG 220 kV Gould Circuit; Jungle-MUX Fiber Optic Upgrades; SCADA/OMS/DMS upgrades; Mobile Substation protection, housing, and station upgrades; substation equipment specifications; EV charging infrastructure at Aquatic Center, Sunset Reservoir, and Del Mar Garage; the Avon Ramp and Arroyo Charging Depots Progressive Design-Build project; Municipal Solar, Energy Storage, and Resilience Projects; System Impact Studies for Large Resource Interconnections; System Modeling for Compliance Studies; TMG Receiving Station capacity studies; and Subtransmission System short-circuit current reduction studies. This list is illustrative and does not constitute a guarantee that any particular project or assignment will be issued under the resulting contracts. Proposers must demonstrate, at a minimum, five (5) years of relevant experience and at least five (5) completed projects within the past five (5) years for each Scope of Work Group proposed. Consultant staff shall include engineers registered in the State of California in the relevant disciplines, including civil, electrical, structural, mechanical, control systems, and/or fire protection engineering, as applicable to the services being performed. Specific minimum qualifications for each Scope of Work Group are stated in Section 6.

opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena is seeking a vendor to provide an Enterprise Monitoring solution and associated implementation and support services. The City seeks a unified monitoring and observability platform that provides centralized visibility across infrastructure, networks, cloud services, databases, applications, integrations, and business services. opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — City of Pasadena, CA
opportunities.title: Wood Pole Inspection, Treatment, Repair, and UAV Inspection Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena Water and Power Department (“PWP”) is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide wood pole inspection, repair, restoration, treatment, and related reporting services for PWP’s electric distribution system. The selected firm will support PWP’s ongoing maintenance and compliance program for wood poles, including visual inspections, intrusive inspections, groundline inspections, preservative treatments, minor corrective repairs, pole reinforcement recommendations, installation of approved repair materials, and detailed reporting of observed conditions. PWP’s wood pole program is intended to support safe, reliable, and compliant operation of the electric distribution system in accordance with applicable requirements, including California Public Utilities Commission (“CPUC”) General Order 95, Rules for Overhead Electric Line Construction, and CPUC General Order 165, Inspection Requirements for Electric Distribution and Transmission Facilities. PWP’s system includes approximately 11,000 wood poles, including both municipally owned and jointly owned poles. A significant portion of the pole population is located in rear property or otherwise constrained access locations. The scope of services may include, but is not limited to, pole condition assessment, identification of structural damage or decay, inspection for General Order 95 infractions, groundline and below-ground inspections, preservative and fumigant treatment, installation of visibility strips, guy guards, ground molding, pole tags, and steel truss reinforcement where approved by PWP. The selected firm shall also provide detailed inspection records, photographs, condition ratings, repair recommendations, and electronic data deliverables in a format acceptable to PWP. In addition to conventional field inspection and treatment services, PWP intends to include drone or other unmanned aerial vehicle (“UAV”) inspection services under the resulting contract. UAV services may be used to supplement field inspections, improve access to difficult or hazardous locations, document pole-top conditions, capture high-resolution imagery, and support more efficient assessment of pole attachments, crossarms, hardware, conductors, insulators, and other visible overhead facilities. UAV services shall be performed by qualified, FAA-compliant personnel and in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements. The selected firm shall furnish all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, vehicles, tools, technology, software, transportation, permits, methods, processes, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the final scope of services, applicable laws and regulations, industry standards, and PWP requirements.

opportunities.title: On-Call Parking Consultant Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena Department of Transportation is soliciting proposals from qualified consulting firms to provide on-call parking consultant services across its portfolio of parking assets and programs. This includes eight City-owned parking garages, four municipal surface lots, approximately 400 multispace meters, five meter districts, parking enforcement operations and comprehensive residential, daytime, and overnight parking permit programs. Selected proposers will form an on-call bench and will be eligible to support infrastructure evaluation, operational studies, technology modernization, and strategic planning and other related activities on an as-needed basis. A minimum of three (3) years experience in such projects is required. Proposers are encouraged to focus on the areas of strength and are not required to team with a large number of sub-consultants to cover all potential types of projects. This Request for Proposals (RFP) does not solicit services for a single, defined project. Rather, the resulting consultant list will be used by the Department of Transportation to assign project-specific Task Orders for parking consulting services required for the City's Parking Division. Each Task Order will define the scope, deliverables, schedule, and coordination needs for the required work. To be considered for selection, consultants must demonstrate substantial experience preparing infrastructure evaluations, operational studies, technology modernization, and strategic planning and other related activities. Consultants selected through this RFP will be placed on an on-call bench available to support the Parking Division's needs on an as-needed basis. Placement on the on-call bench does not guarantee any minimum or maximum number of assignments.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Commercial Real Estate Lease Comparable Database Subscription for San Mateo County Assessor
opportunities.description: The San Mateo County Assessor’s Office invites qualified vendors to submit proposals for unlimited access to digital commercial real estate lease comparable data through an online interface (the “Lease Database”). The resulting subscription will run from January 1 through December 31, 2027, and must provide comprehensive coverage of San Mateo County and the broader San Francisco Bay Area. Commercial appraisal staff will use the Lease Database to support mass appraisal valuations of commercial properties under the income approach to value. Located in Redwood City, California, the Assessor’s Office serves the residents and property owners of San Mateo County by valuing residential, commercial, industrial, and special-purpose properties for property tax assessment purposes. Depending on the property and the appraisal assignment, the Assessor’s Office may use one or more of the three recognized approaches to value: sales comparison, income, and cost. Valuation or reassessment may be required following a change in ownership, completion of new construction, or decline in market value. Because each approach relies on credible market or cost information, the Assessor’s Office contracts with providers of sales and property data, lease data, and construction-cost data covering San Mateo County and neighboring counties. Within this framework, reliable commercial lease comparables are essential to the application of the income approach. The data allow appraisal staff to analyze market rents and lease terms, select appropriate comparables, and document and support their valuation conclusions. This support becomes particularly important when a property owner questions a reassessed value or files a formal appeal with the County Assessment Appeals Board. The selected Lease Database must therefore be comprehensive, defensible, scalable, and suitable for application across the county’s diverse commercial property base. Although the Assessor’s Office’s current lease-data provider has met its operational needs, the Assessor’s Office is conducting a competitive solicitation for the upcoming contract term. This process will allow the Assessor’s Office to evaluate available Lease Databases and select the solution that best satisfies its data, coverage, functionality, access, training, and support requirements while providing the best overall value.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — City of Pasadena, CA
opportunities.title: Rental Registry Database and Portal
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena Rent Stabilization Department is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to provide a comprehensive rental registry database and online portal. The selected vendor will be responsible to meet the City's need for implementing, operating, and maintaining a system that supports the requirements of City Charter Article XVIII, which governs rent stabilization in Pasadena. The Department requires a fully hosted online platform that enables landlords to register rental units, update unit and tenancy information, apply for exemptions, and pay the City’s annual rental registry fee, including any applicable late fees. The system must also allow landlords to submit any rent registration-related notices or documents mandated by the Charter or any applicable federal, state, or local laws directly to the City through the registry portal. A Rental Registry is a core, foundational tool to monitor compliance with Charter Article XVIII to ensure that rent adjustments are in compliance with local law. There are approximately 26,000+ rental units registered within the City of Pasadena Rent Stabilization Department's Rental Registry. Rental property owners are required to register on annual basis and pay a registration fee for each rental unit. Exemptions for the annual registration fee are available and processed through the Rental Registry. Outside of the annual rental registration window from September-October, rental property owners are required to utilize the system to record key events including, but not limited to, occupancy amendments, rent increases and transfer of ownerships. The Rent Stabilization launched its Rental Registry on September 2024. It contains data for approximately 26,000+ rental units. Online payments can be made via eCheck and through Payroc via debit/credit card. A key desire for the next system is to integrate with Tyler Cashiering. The top 3 highest scoring proposals will be invited to participate in product demonstrations during the week of December 7-10, 2026. City Charter Article XVIII can be accessed via this link: https://library.municode.com/ca/pasadena/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=CH_ARTXVIIIPAFAEQHOCHAM . Adopted regulations concerning rental registration, Chapter 9, are available on the Pasadena Rent Stabilization Website via this link: https://www.cityofpasadena.net/rent-stabilization/notices-forms-resources/#regulations

The work to be done consists, in general, of providing all labor, materials, tools, appurtenances, and equipment required as well as any other items and details not mentioned but required by the Contract Documents and as directed by the Director of Public Works or the Director's designee. The target start date and term for the proposed services are subject to negotiation of a final agreement, through the completion of the projects. The Department intends to bring under contract up to two (2) contractors to provide Project Title services with an aggregate fiscal obligation not to exceed $1,000,000 for each agreement during a maximum individual term of one (1) year. Separate Job Orders-Notice to Proceed will be issued under each agreement, as warranted. The apparent lowest, responsive, and responsible bidder shall be selected for consideration for award of each JOC but will be excluded from consideration for each successive contract.
